contract: LLM calls scripts per this manifest; re-implementing the same purpose on the fly is forbidden.

scripts.name: audit_sections.py
scripts.output_contract: stdout JSON {sections, reconcile}; errors: one [ERR] marker line + JSON error object on stderr, exit 2

scripts.name: gen_xlsx.py
scripts.args: --spec <json> --out <xlsx>; spec JSON keys: candidates/measured/notes; candidates and measured are row arrays whose first row is the header; notes is an array of strings
scripts.output_contract: three-sheet xlsx: Candidates/Measured/Notes, written atomically (tmp file + rename, never a partial workbook at the output path); spec validation is all-at-once - every issue collected as error.errors[] ({loc,type,msg,fix}) in one [ERR] payload on stderr, exit 2; missing openpyxl reports through the same [ERR] payload

scripts.name: gen_function_spec.py
scripts.purpose: design-time function spec page generation (the page is generated, never hand-built)
scripts.args: --spec <json> --out <html> [--alignment <json>] [--ladder <json>]; spec JSON keys: topic (str, required), lang ("en"|"zh", default en), decisions (non-empty array of {seq, stage, decision, why, lands, probe, evidence, api}; lands is a string or an array of strings; why and lands optional; probe optional = path to the decision's support-probe document, rendered as a design-time link in the Evidence block; evidence optional = array of probe quote lines (file:line or command output) rendered under the probe link; api optional = the confirmed capability name; VALIDATION: an S3/S4 decision carrying neither probe nor evidence refuses generation), criteria (optional array of {cid, tag, criterion, verify}); --alignment JSON ({"alignment": [{seq, question, decision}]}) writes <out-stem>-decision-log.html (the alignment table: Seq/Question/Decision with OK/Pending status); --ladder JSON ({"ladder": [{version, title, decision, changes, snapshot}]}) writes <out-stem>-version-ladder.html (five fixed fields per round; snapshot paths resolve against the ladder JSON folder and a missing snapshot file refuses generation)
scripts.output_contract: the function spec page plus, when --alignment/--ladder are passed, the two dock tab fragments (<out-stem>-decision-log.html, <out-stem>-version-ladder.html); design-time only, never implemented into production; validation is all-at-once (one [ERR] payload with error.errors[] on stderr, no output file on failure)

scripts.name: gen_verify_script.py
scripts.purpose: per-version deployment regression scaffold (criteria pool 8/16/18): the generated verify script is committed with the version tag and refuses to pass until its click-through steps are filled
scripts.output_contract: writes verify_<version>.py pre-wired with: version parity (the deployed dock must carry the version tag), baseline (with --prev-snapshot: confirmed markup survives verbatim on the deployed page), and a CLICKTHROUGH_FILLED = False flag over the per-version behaviour-steps skeleton - the generated script exits 2 with [ERR]+JSON while the flag is False, so an empty gate is never a fake gate (fill the steps, flip the flag); validation is all-at-once (version/url/snapshot/out issues as error.errors[] on stderr, exit 2)

scripts.name: validate_artifact.py
scripts.purpose: artifact page standards audit (pre-launch gate: the artifact server starts only after this passes); also the deployed-page verify executor for the criteria pool's icon, divider, Title Case and motion audits
scripts.output_contract: exit 0: stdout '[OK] artifact standards passed (n checks)'; failure: one [ERR] marker line + JSON {"error":{"errors":[{loc,type,msg,fix}]}} on stderr listing every failed element at once, exit 2 - the same contract covers argparse failures and undecodable (non-UTF-8) input files, so the gate never crashes bare; checks: icons (every button and h1-h6 carries an icon - the element itself, one of its children, or its immediately preceding sibling is an svg, a [data-icon] element or an icon class; emoji glyphs in page text count as icon failures, zero allowed), dividers (hr and divider-class elements zero unless inside a repeated entry list or their id is in --exempt), dock (a dock element exists, collapsed by default, with exactly four tabs: design preview / function spec / decision log / version ladder), titles (every heading and button renders Title Case, English copy only - --lang zh skips this check), motion (at least one transition or animation declared, every duration inside 80-450 ms read from transition/animation declarations only after stripping CSS comments - comments and transition-delay never fail the check - and a prefers-reduced-motion rule present; static lower bound - per-element coverage is judged in the S5 sweep), tokens (identical element kinds carry identical tokens: one class declares exactly one background value; interactive elements take colors from var(--...) tokens, never raw values), baseline (with --baseline <prev-snapshot>: append-only growth against the previous round's snapshot - the confirmed markup survives verbatim as substring or line-level subsequence, changed or removed confirmed lines are reported as type baseline), behaviour (a page carrying button controls declares behaviour - at least one script element; controls with no script are a drawn mockup and are refused - the static lower bound, the real proof is the deployed click-through per criteria pool 16), coverage (with --spec-data/--round-answers/--snapshots: the deterministic round-close gate - every confirmed answer qid must exist as a decision seq in the spec data (else type spec), a decision citing a probe document must have that file on disk beside the spec data (else type probe: missing probe document), and every answered round N must have snapshot-rN.html in the snapshots folder (else type ladder) - aligned-but-unwritten decisions are refused), version (with --expect-version <tag>: the dock trigger must carry exactly that version tag - build version and prototype version are the same number; a mismatch or an absent dock is reported as type version)

exit 0: stdout '[OK] artifact standards passed (n checks)'; failure: one [ERR] marker line + JSON {"error":{"errors":[{loc,type,msg,fix}]}} on stderr listing every failed element at once, exit 2 - the same contract covers argparse failures and undecodable (non-UTF-8) input files, so the gate never crashes bare; checks: icons (every button and h1-h6 carries an icon - the element itself, one of its children, or its immediately preceding sibling is an svg, a [data-icon] element or an icon class; emoji glyphs in page text count as icon failures, zero allowed), dividers (hr and divider-class elements zero unless inside a repeated entry list or their id is in --exempt), dock (a dock element exists, collapsed by default, with exactly four tabs: design preview / function spec / decision log / version ladder), titles (every heading and button renders Title Case, English copy only - --lang zh skips this check), motion (at least one transition or animation declared, every duration inside 80-450 ms read from transition/animation declarations only after stripping CSS comments - comments and transition-delay never fail the check - and a prefers-reduced-motion rule present; static lower bound - per-element coverage is judged in the S5 sweep), tokens (identical element kinds carry identical tokens: one class declares exactly one background value; interactive elements take colors from var(--...) tokens, never raw values), baseline (with --baseline <prev-snapshot>: append-only growth against the previous round's snapshot - the confirmed markup survives verbatim as substring or line-level subsequence, changed or removed confirmed lines are reported as type baseline)

exit_codes.2: one or more checks failed, or argument error

scripts.name: serve_decision.py
scripts.args: batch: --spec <json> [--round <n>] [--port <n>=8765] [--answers <file>] [--static-root <dir>] [--no-open] / server: --round <n> [--port <n>=8765] [--title <str>] [--options <csv>] [--links <name|url,...>] [--answers <file>] [--no-open] / watcher (fallback only, for orchestrators that cannot watch the server task): --watch <file> --session <token> [--timeout <sec>] (no timeout by default)
scripts.output_contract: GET / serves a UTF-8 multi-card decision page in stepper mode: one card visible at a time, picking an option auto-advances to the next card (~650ms, cancelled by any pointerdown inside the card, note focus, a card switch, or opening the image lightbox), ArrowLeft/ArrowRight slide between cards, ArrowUp/ArrowDown move option focus (Enter/1-9 also pick), a Next-card button appears on decided cards (Review answers on the last one) for mouse parity; page-level side arrows sit fixed at the viewport edges (left = previous card, right = next card or the review panel), disabled at the ends, ArrowUp/ArrowDown move option focus (Enter/1-9 also pick), the option details are always expanded (no hover-expand, no hover motion), images keep natural size (rendered right after the delta caption; clicking opens a lightbox that owns the keyboard - Escape closes) and the page scrolls vertically with a sticky keys hint bar that swaps to submit-oriented hints on the review panel; show() resets scroll to top and focuses the active card (aria-live region announces position); blocking errors render as an in-flow error bar above the cards (never covering card text; nudges auto-hide after 1.8s); after the last card a review panel lists card title + chosen label + write-in text for custom answers (2-line clamp) with pencil Edit links and the single Submit button. Pre-launch the answers sink is probed for writability (a directory or unwritable path refuses with [ERR] + exit 2 before the port binds - a completed round never dies at submit time) and the port fallback never exceeds 65535. UI/UX follows the user's approved reference spec, when provided: gradient page background, sticky top bar with a prominent progress bar and a 'Card n / total' counter, a three-card KPI row under the bar (Cards / Decided / Pending - colored top borders, big numbers, click jumps to the first card of that kind), the alignment table collapsed into a hover strip (hover or focus expands it with a spring grid-rows transition; the strip title stays visible; the expanded fold keeps a faint continuous side/bottom frame joined to the strip; the Pending/Decided chips carry the clock/check icon in both the server-rendered table and the JS-synced cells), card navigation arrows in each card header bar (edge arrows are gone), a card-enter animation on card switch, button micro-transitions, all disabled under prefers-reduced-motion, per-card header band, question block with a blue left edge and no background fill (bold text only), purple recommended tag, slim option rows, bold key content). All icons come from ONE inline SVG line-icon set (help/doc/list/spark/pencil/arrow/clipboard/check/clock/box/eraser/undo/redo, 2px round-cap strokes) - emoji are never used as UI icons. Per card: title, question block (topic title + decision-ask subtitle extracted from the context's ask-label line - the single ask surface, rendered as the card's prominent novice-phrased question (accent-tinted band, bold), Explanation block (remaining context lines as bullets), Options header, 2-3 radio options (asking template: 'N. 65% [RECOMMENDED] label' with the neutral probability chip - tooltip explains the number, optional prob_label legend, probability-descending order when 'probability' present - a probability in (0,1] is read as a fraction and scaled to percent (0.8 renders 80%) - and a Reason/Example/Pros/Cons detail block (why/example strings, pros/cons string arrays) plus delta note and annotated image via /img at natural aspect ratio, image last as evidence; the recommended option carries its RECOMMENDED tag in the list itself, no recap line below; spec authors must avoid bare <...> placeholders in user-visible text (they render literally and read like a broken page) and the write-in input inside the last option is the card's one and only comment field (no per-card note field); context/delta/why/example accept a string or an array of strings (an array is joined with newlines) and render one structured bullet per line (bold lead labels from the short-CJK-label-before-colon convention, example boxes for the example label, **bold** spans, backslash paths as code; plain lines stay plain bullets; a line starting 'N.' renders as an ordered, left-aligned item with its number bolded and no bullet dot); radio values stay the raw labels (display numbering is presentation-only). Optional per question: prob_label (legend for the probability chips). Optional top level: lang (page language, default en), topic (the table heading reads 'Topic Design Tree') and alignment (rows of seq, question and decision; decision null means Pending; the table renders at the top of the page, one page per round; a row may carry qid naming a card of this page, whose decision must then be null and which the page fills in live as the card is answered). Accessibility: prefers-reduced-motion disables all transitions; contrast AA on kicker/badge text. POST /answer with a valid body -> atomic write to the --answers file (default: answers-round<n>.json in the temp folder) [{qid,choice,note,ts,session}], success banner + 3s countdown auto-close (window.close with fallback text); server prints '[INFO] session <token>' before '[OK] serving'; watcher: entries that carry --session appear -> [OK] answers ready + content, exit 0; open the URL from the [OK] serving stdout line, never the requested --port (bind moves to port+1 on conflict); option "url" renders as an open-in-tab link right above the capture (label from the chrome table, capability-named per user ruling: view and annotate in the interactive interface) (an absolute http url of the artifact server, or a bare relative path under --static-root - the console adds the /static/ prefix itself; a leading /static/ prefix or a missing target file is a load error with a corrective fix); a relative url opens annotate-capable in one click (url + ?annotate=1, pencil icon): pages served from --static-root with that flag carry the amber annotation overlay - the page opens with the toolbar ready (every toolbar button carries an inline SVG icon); the action bar sits bottom-right, grouped: AI-marks group, annotation counter, Annotate toggle, user actions, and a separate top tools bar carries the tool group plus undo and redo, shown only while Annotate is on (the tools render icon-only with names in title and aria-label; on the drawn boxes a corner resize grip shows while Annotate is on - dragging the grip resizes the box); every structural annotation step (add, erase, resize) is undoable and redoable - toolbar buttons on the tools bar plus Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y and Ctrl+Shift+Z keyboard parity, disabled buttons on empty stacks, and the option's spec boxes ride along as red AI-mark boxes numbered + labelled, scaled to the page width (each with an x to erase it; clear-all and restore buttons; the remaining AI boxes are baked into the saved capture; behaviour identical in greenfield and refinement); AI marks come in four kinds - box, move, icon and color: box = the red rectangle; move = a dashed arrow from..to with the caption riding the midpoint (a positional change drawn, never described); icon = the suggested icon rendered as a real SVG element on a small card at the spot; color = current and suggested swatches side by side with a small grey hex line under each (the colors are seen, never read as codes - the codes stay in the spec for implementation); the loader validates each kind (move needs from and to {x,y} points, icon needs its SVG fragment, color needs current and suggested, unknown kinds are load errors) and only box-kind marks draw as shotboxes on the console capture; while the Eraser tool is on, the AI marks take the pointer so the eraser reaches every kind: the user toggles Annotate, picks a tool (Box / Arrow / Eraser, icon-only buttons), and drags on the live page - Box draws a frame, Arrow draws a line with an arrowhead and a caption at the tip, Eraser removes any user mark or AI mark on click (Enter inside a caption finishes it, it never submits) (Enter inside a caption finishes that annotation, it never submits) (auto-numbered badges, editable caption "N: what is this about?"), removes any box, and "Save and replace" (the toolbar's save button) self-captures the whole annotated page as a PNG inside the browser (toolbar hidden, caption texts baked into the DOM; on capture failure it degrades to notes-only with a toast), then postMessages {grillSave:{q,o,image,notes}} to the console tab (the href carries &q=<card>&o=<option>), which swaps that option's evidence capture for the annotated PNG (the red evidence boxes are removed with it), returns to that card, checks that option's radio WITHOUT auto-advancing, and renders an eye-catching green badge beside the picked option (circled checkmark, ok palette; annotation-saved lead + click-for-the-next-card action; clicking the badge advances to the next undecided card or the review panel; a quiet "back to console" button closes the tab without saving (focus the console, close; for browsing without annotating), and after a save the annotate tab then returns the user to the console: it focuses the console tab by its window name (the console names its window grill-console; a plain cross-tab focus() is ignored by browsers) and closes itself - the annotate tab opens script-side via window.open so closing is allowed); a generate-prototype button sits beside it: when the user cannot say the change in words, it saves the marks so far (zero marks is fine - the flag itself is the message), postMessages {grillSave:{q,o,image,notes,proto:true}} so the console checks the option, shows the prototype-requested chip on it and renders the green badge with the prototype request message (no auto-advance), and POSTs {url, title, proto:true, boxes:[...]} to /annotations (a bare request with no boxes is accepted, nothing is written, the reply carries proto:true); on Submit the chosen flagged option's answer carries prototypeRequest: true so the agent answers with a generated prototype round (per references/uiux-tree.md: each variant is the real page copied 1:1 with the change applied, every prototype page carries a header tab row with the variant letters and the function spec, feedback regenerates only the commented variant and is re-confirmed, and the confirmed change is implemented 1:1 into the real page while prototype pages never enter the production mirror), and on Submit attaches the PNG (name annotated-capture.png, priority over pasted images, within the 4-image cap) plus the notes (numbered captions joined with "; ") in that answer's images/note fields; the same click also POSTs {url, title, boxes:[{n,x,y,w,h,caption}]} to /annotations, which saves <answers-stem>-annotations.json beside the answers file and prints an [INFO] annotations ready line (the server keeps serving); amber marks the user, the console evidence boxes stay red; one capture per option - no embedded iframe, the live view is one click away; per question "evidence": "rendered" (default; every option carries BOTH its boxed capture and its live url - either half missing is a load error, never a broken page) / "wireframe" (S1 skeleton variants; image or url per option, boxes optional - the wireframe self-annotates) / "degraded" (declared no-render round; renders a STRUCTURAL COMPARISON badge strip on the card); rendered and wireframe both reject at load time any option carrying neither image nor url; every card ends with a renderer-added write-in option (the localized none-of-these choice): picking it focuses a required growing textarea (starts 2 rows, grows with the answer; Enter confirms and advances, Shift+Enter breaks the line), the typed text becomes that card's choice and is stored with the extra key custom: true; Enter inside the write-in input confirms the card and advances (never an implicit form submit), a write-in with images but no text stores the choice as '(image answer)' with its images, and an empty write-in without images at Submit jumps to its card, focuses the field and names the card; every card accepts screenshots via paste or drop: Ctrl+V anywhere in the card, dropping on the paste zone, or click-to-browse there collects up to 4 images per card (max 8 MB each, png/jpg/gif/webp), shown as removable thumbnail chips in the paste zone; on Submit they travel in the answer's "images" key as {name, data dataURL}; the server decodes and saves them beside the answers file (<answers-stem>-<qid-tag>-img<k>.<ext>) and the written answers JSON carries the real file paths in "images" - the paste is the only writer, images land only when the user submits; GET /img serves png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp/bmp/svg; option "image" is a file location on disk - absolute or relative to the spec file (prefer relative so the spec and captures move across machines together), never a web route (/static/...) or http URL: those belong in "url"; resolved and existence-checked at load time (a violation or a missing file is a load error with a corrective hint, never a broken img); an option carrying a screenshot must also carry "boxes": [{x,y,w,h,label?}] in image pixels - the page draws the red circles, numbered badges and red labels over the capture itself, so the region being decided is always marked; after the valid POST the server self-exits: stdout gains '[OK] answers ready: <path>' plus the answers JSON and the process exits 0 - one background task is the whole round, the orchestrator never starts the watcher nor parses the session token; --no-open is a maintainer-check flag: runtime rounds never pass it (the page must open and reach the foreground; per references/uiux-tree.md the orchestrator notifies the user through the question tool) Spec validation is pydantic-style and all-at-once: every issue is collected with a JSON loc path and the [ERR] payload carries error.errors[] = [{loc, type, msg, fix}] listing ALL of them, so the orchestrating model repairs the whole spec in one round-trip. Pre-launch checks run before the port binds or the browser opens: every option url must be openable (a relative url exists as an html file under --static-root; a remote url answers within a bounded probe) and the annotator asset must carry every toolbar button id and format cleanly with the injected keys; any failure prints one [ERR] payload (error.errors[]) and exits 2, and every /static annotate serve re-asserts the button ids before responding. Chrome copy follows the page language: every fixed string the page shows (header subtitle, KPI labels, counters, keys bar, next/review buttons, write-in label and placeholder, paste hint, review panel, option detail leads, aria labels, nudges, paste errors, confirm and error pages, annotation toolbar) renders from the built-in en/zh chrome table selected by the spec lang (zh* -> zh, otherwise en); the JS side reads the same table injected as JSON, and "(image answer)" stays a data-contract literal unchanged by language.

scripts.name: annotate_image.py
scripts.args: --img <png> --out <svg> --box x,y,w,h [--note <text>] (box and note repeatable and pair by order; at least one box; --out must end in .svg - the console serves captures by extension)
scripts.output_contract: writes an SVG embedding the source PNG at natural size with one red box per --box, each carrying a numbered label badge; numbers pair with the --note order and the note text goes to stdout logs only (markers on the artifact, words in the card delta note); boxes are clamped to the image bounds with a [WARN]; extra --note values beyond the box count are dropped with a [WARN] on stdout, never silently; a non-svg --out is refused ([ERR] + JSON, exit 2); the output serves through the console /img endpoint like any png
